intelligence.human_view: Think of it like a reputation score at a club — the more good you bring, the higher it stands. You would never put up a sign saying "reputation points can't be spent as cash" — nobody thought they could, and the sign would only put the idea in their head. You say what the score IS: how much value you brought. Money is a different thing entirely, and it comes its own ways — sharing the network, sharing your own products, sharing your page.
intelligence.simple_view: Points are like gold stars for being helpful! The more good things you do for everyone, the more stars you get! Nobody says stars turn into money — that would be silly! Stars show how much you helped! Money comes when you share good things with people!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — points are your good name, dear, like everyone knowing how much you've helped! You'd never write "good names don't turn into money" on the wall, love — nobody thought that, dear, and writing it only puts the idea in their head! You say what it IS, love — your reputation! Money comes its own ways, dear — sharing the network, sharing your own things, sharing your page!
intelligence.naya_view: A denial is still a mention. "Points never turn into money" puts points and money in the same sentence, in the reader's head, joined — and then denies the join. The reader remembers the join, not the denial. That is why the correction goes further than the old note: not "state it more clearly" but "do not raise it at all". Points have their own positive meaning — reputation, the measure of value brought into the network — and that meaning is the whole frame. Money needs no denial because it lives elsewhere: promoting the network, promoting your own products, sharing your page. Three ways in, none of them through points. The law applies everywhere words about points appear — School round 6 stripped the line from the Q16 board the same call, and the About+Skills round 7 rewrites follow it.
